🍌 When to plant plantain in Nigeria

Also called Ọ̀gẹ̀dẹ̀ àgbagbà (Yoruba) and Ogede (Igbo).

Quick answer: Plant plantain in Nigeria from March to May and harvest from all year round. Suckers are planted early in the rains; bunches are ready about 10–14 months later, so harvest goes on all year.

PlantMarch to May

About plantain

Nigeria is one of the biggest plantain producers in West and Central Africa. Dodo and boli are favourite snacks.

How to plant plantain well

Prop heavy bunches with a pole to stop plants falling.

Suckers are planted early in the rains; bunches are ready about 10–14 months later, so harvest goes on all year.

Diseases and pests of plantain

  • Black Sigatoka (leaf spot)Cut off and destroy infected leaves and plant resistant hybrids (e.g. PITA).
  • Banana weevilPlant clean, pared suckers and keep the field clean.

Best states for plantain

Ondo · Edo · Delta · Rivers · Ogun · Osun · Cross River · Imo · Akwa Ibom · Anambra

Questions farmers ask

When is the best time to plant plantain in Nigeria?

Plant plantain in Nigeria from March to May and harvest from all year round. Suckers are planted early in the rains; bunches are ready about 10–14 months later, so harvest goes on all year.

What is plantain called in Yoruba, Hausa and Igbo?

Plantain is called Ọ̀gẹ̀dẹ̀ àgbagbà (Yoruba) and Ogede (Igbo).

When is plantain harvested in Nigeria?

Plantain is usually harvested from all year round.

Which Nigerian states grow the most plantain?

Ondo, Edo, Delta, Rivers, Ogun, Osun, Cross River, Imo, Akwa Ibom and Anambra are among the best-known plantain states.

Can I grow plantain in my part of Nigeria?

Plantain grows best in the South-West, South-South and South-East regions. In other regions, ask your ADP extension officer before planting.

What diseases attack plantain and how do I prevent them?

Black Sigatoka (leaf spot): Cut off and destroy infected leaves and plant resistant hybrids (e.g. PITA). Banana weevil: Plant clean, pared suckers and keep the field clean.
